title: Follow-up: AppErrorBoundary's fallback UI bakes in a full-page (100vh) layout assumption (PR #83)
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's review of PR #83 (frontend-app-shell-navigation-followups), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so it isn't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: PR #83's move of AppErrorBoundary from components/layout/ to components/common/AppErrorBoundary/ is a correct call per Frontend.md §3 (it's fully domain-agnostic and its catch-a-render-crash behavior is a generic pattern, not app-shell-specific) — the placement itself isn't in question. However, the fallback UI's own markup still bakes in a whole-app assumption: `minHeight: '100vh'` and copy that says 'reload the app' (AppErrorBoundary.tsx render()). The component's own updated doc comment argues it 'could wrap just a feature subtree' in the future, but if it did today, a subtree-scoped instance would render a fallback that's sized and worded for filling the entire viewport, not the bounds of whatever smaller subtree it actually wraps — undercutting the reusability rationale used to justify the common/ placement. Consider parameterizing the fallback (e.g. an optional `fullPage`/`minHeight` prop, or moving the 100vh sizing to the call site in main.tsx) so a future feature-subtree usage doesn't inherit whole-page-sized chrome by default.
